subject: Discovery follow-up: inference cost snapshot, levers, and next asks

Subject: Discovery — inference economics & pilot scope

Camila, thanks for the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side so we're aligned before you send numbers: 

- Primary pain: current LLM vendor spikes meaningfully on peak hours; our monthly spend has been unpredictable and exceeded internal forecasts by ~40% in two of the last four months.
- SLA/latency target: 95th pct < 350ms for single-response chat flows, some batch reranking jobs can tolerate 2–5s.
- Regulatory: customer PII must not leave our VPC for some workloads; we may require Private deployment for final production.
- Budget: procurement flagged a target of ~$25k/month for the first-stage pilot (proof-of-value).
- Usage shape: ~80k user queries/month today, highly spiky (2–3x on market open). Average request ~120 tokens in/out, top 5% are long dialogs ~600 tokens.

Can you confirm if Redwood can show a realistic TCO for a 6-week pilot that keeps us under the indicated budget (or clearly shows what tradeoffs are needed)? Also want to understand: batching/caching levers, rough hosted vs dedicated delta, and what data points you need from us to firm numbers.

Appreciate a crisp next steps doc. Will loop procurement (procurement@greenbank.com) after we have an estimate.

—Sam
VP Product, GreenBank

Sam — thanks for the clear recap. Below is what we'll deliver in a follow-up packet and the immediate asks from your side to make the cost estimates accurate. Attaching a quick cost workbook (redwood_quickcost_v1.xlsx) that contains the same high-level numbers summarized below.

Short summary (pilot hypothesis)
- Pilot length: 6 weeks; two models: a chat model for customer-facing flows and a reranker for search relevance.
- Pilot target traffic (scope): 100k queries/month, average 120 tokens/request, peak concurrency ~1.2k QPS during spikes (traffic bursts ~10 minutes).
- Goal: validate both latency SLOs and confirm net unit cost improvements using caching and batching levers.

Quick TCO snapshot (hosted, rough estimate)
- Naive hosted cost (no caching/batching): ~$38k/month (model size + inference tokens).
- With conservative batching & prefix/KV caching applied: estimated ~$22k–$28k/month depending on cache hit rate (15%–40%).
- Dedicated/reserved estimate (small pool + autoscale buffer): one-time setup + commit needed; run-rate after commit: ~$18k/month (with higher predictability and lower per-token unit cost) but requires minimum monthly commitment and time to provision.

Key levers we will model in the workbook and in the pilot:
- Batching: continuous batching for request aggregation during microbursts; increases throughput and reduces per-token cost but can add median latency if not tuned.
- KV/prefix caching: for repeating prompts or session contexts this often yields the largest token savings (we model hit-rates at 15%/25%/40%).
- Quantization & model variants: we can evaluate int8/4-bit quantized variants for reranker; typically 20%–35% token-cost reduction with modest latency improvements.

What we need from GreenBank to tighten numbers
- Historical daily/hourly QPS for the last 30 days (CSV preferred) — needed to model batching effectiveness.
- Distribution of token lengths (percentiles): p50/p90/p95 of prompt + response tokens.
- A couple of representative prompts or a subset of sessions (anonymized) so we can estimate caching hit-rate potential.
- Confirmation whether PII workloads will run in your VPC (affects private deployment estimates).

Next steps (proposed)
1) Ben and I will run the attached quickcost with the ranges above and a small sensitivity analysis.
2) If numbers look viable for you, we propose a 6-week pilot scope and an MAD (mutual action plan) doc — I attached a skeleton (mutual-action-plan.docx).
3) Sam to share the usage histogram and prompt samples; procurement to confirm pilot budget flexibility and approval process.

I'm copying Ben (SE) who will add a short technical note on batching/caching expected gains and an ask for any telemetry format you prefer. We'll aim to send the cost workbook + playbook tomorrow EOD.

Best,

Adding the technical perspective and a couple of concrete numbers so Sam's team can sanity-check quickly. Attaching a short playbook (batching-playbook.pdf).

Technical notes (summary):
- Batching mechanics: for microbursts, continuous batching can aggregate small requests into efficient GPU kernels. If average request latency allowance >= 30–50ms for aggregation, we typically see 15%–30% per-token cost reduction on chat models. For rerankers, batching gives up to 40% throughput improvement because the model execution is dense.
- KV/prefix caching: if 20% of requests hit cached KV entries (session reuse, repeated prompts), token savings map almost 1:1 to cost savings on the response side. Example: 100k requests/month at 120 tokens = 12M tokens; 20% cache hit on responses reduces billed tokens to ~9.6M — ~20% net token cost reduction.
- Quantized model variants: moving the reranker to int8 often reduces runtime and can drop per-token cost another 15%–25%; we validate for accuracy regression in a short eval.
- Latency tradeoffs: with careful scheduling we can keep 95th pct under 350ms while still batching; we instrument tail-latency and set dynamic batch-size caps to respect SLOs.

Rough worked example (numbers to put in workbook):
- Baseline (no levers): 12M tokens/month => hosted cost ~$38k/month (ballpark).
- Apply batching (20% effective): tokens billed equivalent -> 9.6M => hosted cost ~$30k/month.
- Apply caching (20% response hits) on top of batching: billed tokens ~7.7M => hosted cost ~$24k/month.
- Dedicated commit can reduce per-token spend another ~15% after amortizing reserved capacity + improved kernel/throughput scheduling => ~$20k/month.

Pilot instrumentation asks (minimal):
- Provide 30 days of token histograms and an example session trace (anonymized).
- A test API key or export method so Redwood can replay a small sample set in our staging to measure cache-hit and batch efficiency quickly.

We will run two sensitivity lines in the workbook: conservative (10% cache, 10% batching), realistic (20% cache, 20% batching), optimistic (35% cache, 25% batching).

Happy to join a quick call to walk through the workbook when you have shared the data.

—Ben
